cases.answer: Decision: the auth service issues short-lived access tokens (15 minutes) with rotating refresh tokens, and all public clients use PKCE [doc:confluence:7201]. Rejected alternative: long-lived opaque sessions in the database, because they make revocation cheap but every API call pays a database round trip [doc:confluence:7201]. Michelle Lim: Auth service design: proposal is short-lived access tokens with rotating refresh tokens, PKCE everywhere, revocation list in Redis [doc:slack:C0AUTH:1789568549.000700]. Follow-up from the Q2 payment outage postmortem [doc:jira:PAY-231]. Replace the manual paygw-rotate runbook step with a scheduled job that rotates the acquirer mTLS client certificate 14 days before expiry and alerts if rotation fails [doc:jira:PAY-231]. The payment gateway is a stateless Go service in ap-southeast-1 behind an internal load balancer [doc:confluence:8813]. It terminates merchant TLS, validates requests, and forwards to the acquirer through an mTLS upstream whose client certificate is rotated every 90 days [doc:confluence:8813]. Root cause: the acquirer mTLS client certificate on the payment gateway expired at 03:00 and rotation was a manual runbook step that nobody was paged for [doc:gdrive:1postmortemQ2]. Follow-ups: PAY-231 automates the certificate rotation with a scheduled job, and PAY-232 adds a synthetic checkout probe so a gateway 502 pages within two minutes [doc:gdrive:1postmortemQ2]. Ho Ming: Upstream mTLS client certificate expired at 03:00 [doc:slack:C0INC:1783952549.000400].
